newsitem.title: BARBADOS: Barbados, U.S. could sign drug pact soon.
newsitem.headline: Barbados, U.S. could sign drug pact soon.

text.p: Barbadian officials said on Thursday they could be prepared to sign a drug interdiction pact with the United States immediately after President Bill Clinton meets Caribbean leaders on Saturday.

Prime Minister Owen Arthur told journalists that there has been progress in talks this week between his government and U.S. drug czar Gen. Barry McCaffrey, and "there will be a signing in due course."

Deputy Prime Minister Billie Miller, speaking at a separate press briefing, stated the talks are "virtually at closure" and it was likely a submission could be made to the cabinet on Friday that would allow for a signing on Saturday.

Barbados has so far refused to sign the so-called "shiprider" agreement that has already been signed by most other countries in the region, stating the pact would infringe on its sovereignty. The accord would allow U.S. officials to interdict air and sea craft and apprehend suspects.
Arthur said his government has been in close collaboration with Jamaica, which announced on Monday that it was prepared to sign a greatly amended version.
According to Jamaica's Prime Minister P.J. Patterson, U.S. authorities will only be allowed into his country's territorial waters and airspace on a "case-by-case" basis.
